title: Arbitrary DVR base change of a local unramified field compositum
statement: Let $R,V,A,T$ be DVR domains [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Suppose $R\to V$ is local and injective, essentially of finite type [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra], and formally unramified (its module of relative Kahler differentials is zero). Give $A$ a local $R$-algebra structure and $T$ a local $A$-algebra structure. Let $k:V\to T$ be a ring map agreeing on $R$ with $R\to A\to T$. Let $F$ be a field [def-pc-field-extension] and an $A$-algebra, and make it the fraction field of $T$, compatibly with $A$. Let $i_V:\operatorname{Frac}(V)\to F$ be a field map satisfying $i_V(v)=k(v)$ in $F$ for every $v\in V$. Suppose the $A$-subalgebra generated by $i_V(\operatorname{Frac}(V))$ is all of $F$. Then $T$ is essentially of finite type and formally unramified over $A$. No locality of $k$, no finiteness of $A/R$, and no uniformizer-root or tame ramification hypotheses are assumed.

source.place: Tag 09EQ, tensor and local-factor proof, extended directly to arbitrary local DVR base change; Tags 09E7 and 02FM.

proof.text: Form D=A tensor_R V and its compatible map phi:D->T. Let Q=phi^-1(m(T)) and S=D_Q. Extend phi to g:S->T and prove g is local by the numerator unit criterion; its composite with A is the original local map.

Faithfulness makes V flat over R. Flatness, essential finite type, and formal unramifiedness survive tensor base change and localization. The local unramified criterion gives m(A)S=m(S). The closed source theorem IsRegularLocalRing.of_flat_of_map_maximalIdeal_eq proves S regular local, hence a domain. A nonzero image of a uniformizer of A generates m(S), so the proved principal maximal ideal criterion makes S a DVR.

Compatibility with the field injection iV keeps a base uniformizer of R nonzero in T. Its image in A is a multiple of an A-uniformizer, so that uniformizer also stays nonzero in T. Factorization into uniformizer powers proves g is injective.

Extend V->S and S->T->F to fraction fields. Uniqueness of fraction-field lifts gives the composite Frac(V)->Frac(S)->F=iV. The range of Frac(S)->F contains A and iV(Frac(V)); the adjoin generation hypothesis therefore makes it all of F. Thus F is also the fraction field of S.

Apply Mathlib bijective_rangeRestrict_comp_of_valuationRing to g and T->F. It makes g surjective. Algebra.EssFiniteType.of_surjective and Algebra.FormallyUnramified.of_surjective give both claimed properties for T.

theorem dvr_unramified_compositum_base_change
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsDiscreteValuationRing R]
    (V : Type u) [CommRing V] [IsDomain V] [IsDiscreteValuationRing V]
    [Algebra R V] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R V)] [FaithfulSMul R V]
    [Algebra.EssFiniteType R V] [Algebra.FormallyUnramified R V]
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsDiscreteValuationRing A]
    [Algebra R A] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R A)]
    (T : Type u) [CommRing T] [IsDomain T] [IsDiscreteValuationRing T]
    [Algebra A T] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap A T)]
    (k : V →+* T)
    (hR : ∀ r : R, k (algebraMap R V r) = algebraMap A T (algebraMap R A r))
    (F : Type u) [Field F] [Algebra A F] [Algebra T F]
    [IsFractionRing T F] [IsScalarTower A T F]
    (iV : FractionRing V →+* F)
    (hiV : ∀ v : V, iV (algebraMap V (FractionRing V) v) = algebraMap T F (k v))
    (hgen : Algebra.adjoin A (Set.range iV) = ⊤) :
    Algebra.EssFiniteType A T ∧ Algebra.FormallyUnramified A T
